messages:
anya: noticing a spike in duplicate token charges when clients reconnect after a proxy 503. happened across multiple tenants this morning. :bug:
sam: do you have a repro or trace id?
anya: yes — trace=trace-9f1d. pattern: client opens SSE -> proxy 503 -> client reconnects quickly -> server accepts and resumes but billing shows 2 partial sessions for same resume-id.
michael: that sounds like the resume idempotency window not aligning with quota billing window. billing counts sessions when route switch completes. if resume completes after rollback, we double-count.
joanna: hmm, telemetry shows the resume handshake sometimes lands after a sticky-route swap. controller emits two 'session_accepted' events with same resume id but different route_ids.
kevin: could also be TCP-level close vs app-level resume ordering. proxy sends 502 then client retries; the old session hasn't been garbage-collected by the runtime yet.
anya: attaching the minimal headers we saw: ```GET /v1/stream?s=xyz Resume-Id: r-12345 X-Route: shard-a``` then later: ```GET /v1/stream?s=xyz Resume-Id: r-12345 X-Route: shard-b```
sam: any reason console metrics didn't flag this? I thought session-dedupe metric would catch duplicate resume ids.
joanna: metric exists but it's per-route. since route changed the dedupe didn't trigger. telemetry team suggested a global resume_id index but worried about scale.
michael: proposal: implement a short "quarantine" period (200-500ms) when a resume arrives on a new route for same resume id. Instead of immediate session acceptance/billing, mark as pending and wait for final session confirmation from previous route or a failover marker. If previous route confirms closed, accept; if not, accept after timeout and attribute legacy overflow with flag.
kevin: quarantine helps but adds latency. clients wanting low p99 might be impacted. can we make it adaptive: quarantine = min(500ms, 5 * avg-reconnect-latency-for-tenant)?
anya: adaptive sounds good. also we should emit a console flag "quarantine_applied" per session so SRE can see affected tenants.
sam: implementation concerns: where to track pending resume ids? centralized index vs sticky-route-coordinator. centralized solves dedupe but adds cross-region writes.
joanna: maybe leverage our existing resume-index in controller (it's sharded by tenant). expand the shard to accept a transient state "pending-route-swap" that auto-expires. should be bounded.
kevin: what about billing? we should prevent incrementing token/session counters until quarantine clears or previous route confirms closure. add a billing-flag "deferred_charge" to avoid double-billing; then reconcile in daily job if both routes charged erroneously.
michael: and add a telemetry event 'quarantine_resolution' with labels: resume_id, outcome=accepted|rejected|timed_out, route_from, route_to, tenant. that will help tune the heuristic.
anya: product ask: console UX — can we expose a lightweight timeline per session showing route hops and whether quarantine applied? customers keep asking why reconnects show extra cost.
sam: agree. product could show a compact view: route timeline + "billing attribution" with hover to explain quarantine.
joanna: opsbot: I can add a quick alert on large count of quarantine_timeouts per tenant to catch misbehaving proxies. opsbot, can you create an onboarding doc?
opsbot: created ticket infra-rt/622: "quarantine heuristic detection & alerting" and a dashboard template.
kevin: one more edge: JWT rotation where resume token is valid on old route but rejected on new route. quarantine needs to check auth status too, otherwise we'll accept a resume then immediately revoke.
michael: good call. check auth validity as part of pending checks. if auth mismatch, reject immediately with 401 so client can refresh.
anya: plan summary: (1) prototype transient pending-state in controller shards, (2) implement adaptive quarantine timer and deferred billing flag, (3) emit telemetry + console flag, (4) add dashboard/alert, (5) UX timeline for customers.
sam: timeline? can we get a prototype in 2 weeks?
joanna: engineering OK for a limited canary: shard-1 in us-west next week, telemetry enabled.
kevin: i'll handle billing deferral and recon jobs, michael can own telemetry, joanna + anya own controller changes, sam + product do console UX.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout: controller/shard-1 on 2450002200 -> 2450002800.
anya: thanks all. i'll paste traces & example charts into the infra ticket. :thumbsup:
kevin: adding unit tests for race conditions and a stress test to the chaos harness.
michael: once canary looks stable we'll tune the adaptive multiplier. leaving notes in infra-rt/622 for follow-up.
anya: great. closing thread for now but will comment with canary results.
